newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW - Ceramco split still a live issue.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ceramco split still a live issue.

text.p: Ceramco Corp Ltd Executive Chairman David Appleby said on Thursday the ceramics and lingerie maker had not closed the door on the possibility of splitting off its two seemingly disparate businesses.
"It's still a pretty live issue and there have got to be arguments to split them up. Clay and lingerie don't seem to be natural partners," Appleby told Reuters in an interview.
Critics have suggested the businesses should be separated but Appleby, a relative newcomer to the board, said it all came down to a question of how to maximise shareholder value.
The loss-making Bendon Hickory lingerie division was not in a condition to stand alone as a public company and the China Clays ceramics division was probably not suitable either.

"The feeling is that we've probably got to do some fundamental corrections to the businesses, get them into a situation where they have got a profit stream, and then review it. That's something that we are looking at at present."
Appleby said Ceramco's new-look board was coming to grips with the issues.

"I think that in the New Year, once we've got on top of Bendon, that it's an issue we will need to look at as to whether we do accept the fact that we should be working towards selling off one of the businesses or splitting them up."
But Appleby said it did not automatically follow that companies with seemingly incongruous operations could not operate successfully under one roof.
He cited Corporate Investments, which makes wine and distributes truck parts, as an example.
And with Ceramco likely to become debt free by mid-1997, it may well build on what it has and move down an acquisition path.

"That's a philosophical issue the board is going to have to address in the middle of next year as to whether it remains as two businesses, sells one off, goes down a different path or acquires more," he said.
"At that stage we will need to make the decision as to what is the best way to increase shareholder value."
"Our feeling has been that we should focus on getting profit back into the business and if you are going to sell them, at least groom them for sale in pretty good nick."
Ceramco, once an investors' favourite, suffered a NZ$1.6 million loss in the six months to September.

The shares, which today traded at NZ$1.15, have been bouncing around historic lows for many months and the company has in the past been severely punished for not meeting its own overly optimistic earnings projections.
But it expects to break even in the current year and return to profitability in 1997/98. Appleby expects the restructuring to be complete by March.
"I think we've got an expectation that hopefully the worst will be behind us after the 1997 year and that we should then be into profit," he said.
"It will not happen immediately but certainly we think we've cut the rot, now it's matter of building from there."
In Australia, Ceramco's Bendon and Hickory sales forces had been merged but there was further streamlining to be done in the whole sales and marketing approach here and in Australia.
Ceramco aims to maintain its high market share in New Zealand lingerie and hopes to advance its share in Australia, particularly with the Elle MacPherson brand.
Appleby has been acting as managing director after the departure of John Baird earlier this year.
The board expects to announce a new managing director to Bendon within four to five weeks.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
